title: Autonomous AI Disproof of Erdős’s 1946 Unit-Distance Conjecture (Problem #90)
whyItMatters: Disproved Paul Erdős’s 80-year-old 1946 unit-distance conjecture; independently verified by nine prominent mathematicians including Timothy Gowers and Melanie Wood.
summary: OpenAI announced that an internal reasoning model autonomously constructed a counterexample disproving Erdős Problem #90 (1946) on unit distances in the plane, synthesizing ideas from Ellenberg–Venkatesh, Golod–Shafarevich, and Hajir–Maire–Ramakrishna. Nine external mathematicians—including Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers and Melanie Wood—published a concise human-verified exposition on arXiv the same day, with Gowers noting that no prior AI-generated proof had come close to top-journal quality.
technicalHighlights: Resolved an 80-year-old problem posed by Paul Erdős in 1946 via an unexpected algebraic-number-theoretic construction.
Independently checked and digested by nine leading mathematicians (Alon et al., arXiv:2605.20695) with day-one transparency.
Widely cited by skeptics and proponents alike as the turning point where AI crossed into genuine top-journal research math.
caveats: OpenAI’s Sebastien Bubeck noted the proof synthesized known deep tools rather than inventing wholly new mathematical theory, and the internal model remains unreleased.
